facts.fact: At the Fair Pritam orders the forty to hold the herald and claims Neshar owes him eleven hundred measures of winter grain. Rohan answers that those are the crown's measures, carry Pritam's store-bell, were hoarded through the closing and sold back to Ranu at famine price; a hill-council man says he paid four times the autumn price for a sack. The officer lowers his spear only after Tej's sword belt lies on the grass. Revises earlier F354 wording.
Meera uses the rope signal of one long pull (come, per F128) to call Rohan away from Ila at the Fair; he leaves his sister mid-sentence and follows.

At the Fair two soldiers take Meera's arms and the herald enters her as 'Meera of Kothi Shilak, called the Salt Fox. Held pending the queen's judgement.' Kunal's 'Hold' stops them removing her; the officer has them release her after the herald is freed. The entry stands in the crown's record. (F353, Ila's 'two hours late', is withdrawn; F308 'eight days late' stands.)
